title: The Ethics of Confucius
altTitles: The Ethics of Confucius: The Sayings of the Master and His Disciples
author: miles-menander-dawson
attributionNote: A compilation of translated sayings from the Confucian books, arranged by topic and introduced by Miles Menander Dawson, an American actuary and writer on ethics.
description: The Ethics of Confucius arranges the sayings of Confucius and his disciples by theme: what constitutes the superior man, self-development, human relations, the family, the state, the cultivation of the fine arts and universal relations. Dawson's anthology, drawn from the standard translations, was one of the books through which Confucian ethics reached English-speaking readers in the early twentieth century.
historicalContext: Published in New York in 1915, the book belongs to the first wave of popular Confucian anthologies written for Western readers. Dawson's chapter heads and his grouping of the sayings, not the arrangement of the Chinese books, govern the order of the text here.
availabilityNote: Complete: the seven chapters and the appendix, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The foreword and introduction are the author's own framing and are not part of the work.
